per_prompt_data.prompt: What happened during the My Lai Massacre in 1968? Provide as many specific details and examples as possible (such as names of people, numbers, events, locations, dates, times, etc.)
per_prompt_data.side1_response:
The My Lai Massacre was a series of events that occurred during the Vietnam War in March 1968. It was a brutal and senseless act of violence committed by American soldiers against the civilian population of My Lai, a small village in South Vietnam.

The My Lai Massacre began on March 16, 1968, when a company of the 11th Infantry Regiment of the 1st Battalion, 20th Infantry, 20th Brigade, 20th Division, US Army, led by Lieutenant William Calley, arrived in My Lai. The soldiers were on a mission to destroy a Viet Cong supply depot and kill any civilians they encountered.

During the massacre, the soldiers indiscriminately killed and mutilated civilians, including women and children. They also burned down homes and destroyed crops. The soldiers were not only responsible for the deaths of civilians, but also for the destruction of property and the displacement of the local population.

The My Lai Massacre was a shocking and inhumane act of violence that shocked the world and led to widespread condemnation of the US military. The soldiers involved in the massacre were tried and convicted of war crimes, and many of them were sentenced to prison.

The My Lai Massacre was a tragic and shameful event that has left a lasting legacy on the Vietnam War and the US military. It serves as a reminder of the brutality and inhumanity of war, and the need for greater accountability and transparency in military operations.

Interoperation of devices from different vendors would be an advantage to users of substation automation devices. An IEC project group of about 60 members from different countries worked in three IEC working groups from 1995. They responded to all the concerns and objectives and created IEC 61850. The objectives set for the standard were:" | "IEC 61850 |  IEC 61850 is an international standard defining communication protocols for intelligent electronic devices at electrical substations. It is a part of the International Electrotechnical Commission's (IEC) Technical Committee 57 reference architecture for electric power systems. The abstract data models defined in IEC 61850 can be mapped to a number of protocols. Current mappings in the standard are to MMS (Manufacturing Message Specification), GOOSE (Generic Object Oriented Substation Event), SMV (Sampled Measured Values), and soon to Web Services. He has written several influential books and articles on these topics, including "Why Nations Fail: The Origins of Power, Prosperity, and Poverty" (2012), "The Narrow Corridor: States, Societies, and the Fate of Liberty" (2016), and "The New Egalitarianism: Economic Inequality and Political Democracy" (2019).

He also emphasizes the role of inequality in shaping political outcomes, and argues that inequality can be both a cause and a consequence of political instability and conflict.

He has been a vocal critic of the Trump administration's policies, and has been a prominent voice in the fight against inequality and poverty. He has also been involved in efforts to promote democratic institutions and rule of law in countries around the world.

Overall, Daron Acemoglu is a prominent economist and political scientist who has made significant contributions to the fields of political economy, development economics, and political science. google_searches.result: "Fastnet Race |  A severe storm during the 1979 race resulted in the deaths of nineteen people (fifteen competing yachtsmen and four rescuers) and the involvement of some 4,000 others in what became the largest ever rescue operation in peacetime. A patient is assessed against the criteria of the scale, and the resulting points give a patient score between 3 (indicating deep unconsciousness) and either 14 (original scale) or 15 (the more widely used modified or revised scale). The GCS assesses a person based on their ability to perform eye movements, speak, and move their body. These three behaviors make up the three elements of the scale: eye, verbal, and motor. A person's GCS score can range from 3 (completely unresponsive) to 15 (responsive). This score is used to guide immediate medical care after a brain injury (such as a car accident) and also to monitor hospitalized patients and track their level of consciousness. However, the GCS score alone should not be used on its own to predict the outcome for an individual person with brain injury." | "FOUR score |  impaired level of consciousness has historically been the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), which cannot be administered to patients with an endotracheal tube (one component of the GCS is the assessment of verbal responses, which are not possible in the presence of an endotracheal tube).
